banner: MOCK BACKEND, UNCALIBRATED TIMING. These numbers describe the routing policies and the plumbing on a CPU, with placeholder step times (D-008). They are not GPU performance and must not be quoted as such.
command: python -m bench.router_compare --out <redacted> --label load cap sweep: 64 prefixes, 0.25 GB pool per replica, 30 req/s, 1200 requests --seeds 0,1,2 --num-requests 1200 --rate 30 --mock-time-scale 2 --shared-prefix-groups 64 --kv-cache-gb 0.25 --load-caps 4,8,16,32,1000 --policies round-robin,least-outstanding,approx-prefix,precise-prefix
label: load cap sweep: 64 prefixes, 0.25 GB pool per replica, 30 req/s, 1200 requests
notes: Placeholder mock timing (see mock_timing), not calibrated against any real run.
No warm-up: every policy starts with cold caches and pays for its first sight of each prefix.
Fresh replica and router processes for every run; variants of a seed receive the identical workload (see workload_digest).
Run on Windows: sleeps and scheduling here are not those of a Linux box, and the replicas, router and load generator share one machine.
The shared-prefix workload shape (groups, length, skew) is a modelling choice, not a measurement of real traffic.
